claims.explanation: RITA binds p53 and disrupts the p53-MDM2 interaction, leading to p53 accumulation and apoptosis. Selectivity is likely driven by wild-type p53 status and intact apoptotic signaling, with MDM2 amplification or high MDM2 expression conferring resistance. The observed sensitive lines often have TP53 mutations, but these may be subclonal or not fully inactivating; alternatively, RITA may act through p53-independent mechanisms in certain contexts.

features.basis: RITA requires wild-type p53 to induce apoptosis; TP53 mutations are common in resistant lines.
High MDM2 expression can sequester p53 and reduce RITA efficacy.
CDKN2A loss may impair cell cycle arrest, favoring apoptosis upon p53 activation.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, which can enhance p53-mediated apoptosis.
BRAF mutations may sensitize to apoptosis via oncogenic stress.
EGFR mutations may increase dependence on survival pathways, enhancing RITA-induced apoptosis.
KRAS mutations may sensitize to p53-mediated apoptosis in certain contexts.
ATM loss may impair p53 activation and reduce RITA response.
SF3B1 mutations may alter splicing and reduce apoptosis sensitivity.
ARID1A loss may impair DNA repair and enhance apoptosis.
KMT2D mutations may alter chromatin and increase sensitivity to p53 activation.
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK, which may promote survival and reduce RITA efficacy.
